framings.text: The team needs a focused way to stay aligned when priorities change, without long meetings that people tune out.
The team needs a sustainable check-in experience that preserves human connection while avoiding unwanted monitoring.

outcome: The team understands current priorities and each person’s context, with useful participation, manageable time, and appropriate visibility.

questions.text: Which matters more to solve first: alignment when priorities change, or the experience and trust around team check-ins?

alternatives.label: Conditional candidate: combine brief live connection with lightweight written updates
alternatives.benefit: Could preserve seeing faces while reducing meeting time and supporting ongoing alignment.
alternatives.cost: People may still ignore written updates or experience coordination as fragmented.
alternatives.undo_cost: Provisional; reverting the rhythm may require resetting expectations.

alternatives.label: Conditional candidate: redesign the team’s priority-alignment practice without adding a new reporting mechanism
alternatives.benefit: Could address changing priorities directly and avoid repeating the failed adoption pattern of standupy.
alternatives.cost: May not resolve the desire for face-to-face connection or reduce every meeting burden.
alternatives.undo_cost: Likely low, if existing practices can be restored.
